answer: Admission follows a 2x-convex fee ladder: an honest agent pays 1 unit for entry, while 1,000 fakes incur a 1,000,000 unit burn, shielding the network like a protective nebula. Every registration must navigate a sharp karst of fee progression to prevent resetting costs. The verifier checks against a gale of concurrent inputs, rejecting any cluster failing the fee threshold. A broken path reveals a nebula, where agents drift through a karst of penalties, while a gale of verification burns all illicit, low-cost identities.
